purpose: Alprazolam is used to treat anxiety disorders and panic disorder. It helps calm feelings of intense worry, fear, or nervousness. It works quickly and is usually used for short-term relief of anxiety symptoms.
how_it_works: Your brain has a natural calming chemical called GABA. Alprazolam boosts the effect of GABA, which slows down your brain activity and helps you feel more relaxed and less anxious. Think of it like turning down the volume on an overactive nervous system.
common_side_effects: Feeling sleepy or drowsy, dizziness, feeling lightheaded, trouble with memory or concentration, dry mouth, and feeling unsteady on your feet. These effects are more common when you first start taking it.
warnings: This medication can be habit-forming, so it is very important to take it exactly as prescribed and not to stop it suddenly without talking to your doctor first — stopping suddenly can cause serious withdrawal symptoms. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication, as the combination can be very dangerous and even life-threatening. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially other sleep aids or pain medications.
typical_dosing: For anxiety, the usual starting dose is 0.25 mg to 0.5 mg taken 3 times a day. For panic disorder, doses may be higher. Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly adjust it based on how you respond. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you to.
